title: 导论　扩展场域中的中国当代艺术
originalTitle: Introduction: Chinese Contemporary Art in the Expanded Field

en: Introduction: Chinese Contemporary Art in the Expanded Field
zh: 导论　扩展场域中的中国当代艺术

en: At the beginning of the 1990s, no named Chinese artist had ever participated in the Venice Biennale, one of the most prestigious and longest-running international art shows in the world.
In 1999, twenty Chinese artists—the most from any single country—showed more than fifty visual artworks at the Forty-Eighth Biennale.

This historic shift reflected the post-1989 circulation of contemporary art from China in Hong Kong, Japan, Europe, and the United States, as well as the erratic but gradual loosening of political control of art in China. By the early 2000s, Chinese cities such as Beijing, Chengdu, Guangzhou, and Shanghai had adopted the “biennale” model, seen as a marker of cultural cosmopolitanism, and began launching large contemporary art exhibits of their own. During this period of change, an almost uniformly male cohort of artists, noted for their bad boy political dissent, garnered attention on the international museum circuit and art market. Overseas observers heralded their work as representative of reform-era China. Their female counterparts, many of whom had trained alongside them in state-supported art academies, remained in the long shadow cast by this international spotlight on a masculinist avant-garde.
zh: 20世纪90年代初，还没有任何一位具名的中国艺术家参加过威尼斯双年展——这是世界上历史最悠久、最具声望的国际艺术展之一。
1999年，二十位中国艺术家——来自单一国家的人数最多——在第四十八届威尼斯双年展上展出了五十多件视觉艺术作品。

这一历史性转变，反映了1989年之后中国当代艺术在香港、日本、欧洲和美国的流通，也反映了中国对艺术的政治控制虽有起伏却逐步松动。到21世纪初，北京、成都、广州和上海等中国城市已采用“双年展”模式——它被视为文化世界主义的标志——并开始举办自己的大型当代艺术展。在这一变革时期，一批几乎清一色为男性的艺术家以其“坏男孩”式的政治异见闻名，在国际博物馆巡展体系和艺术市场上获得关注。海外观察者称赞他们的作品代表了改革时代的中国。而他们的女性同行——其中许多人曾在国家支持的美术院校与他们一同受训——仍留在国际聚光灯投向男性主义前卫艺术所投下的长长阴影之中。

en: Several contending narratives framed this explosion of Chinese contemporary art on the international stage. Exhibition in the West rescued and recuperated Chinese artists suppressed by an authoritarian government. Or, this phenomenon represented a radical reversal of socialist China’s art system and new opening to “the world.” Or, it demonstrated China’s national triumph on the global cultural scene. Indeed, by 2005, China had its own national pavilion at the Venice Biennale.
By 2011, when India organized its first pavilion, anxiety crept into Western reportage. The

’s coverage of this moment leads with a vaguely accusatory tone: “Not content with their status as nascent economic superpowers, China and India are set to storm a very European cultural bastion, the Venice Biennale.”
zh: 关于中国当代艺术在国际舞台上的爆发，有几种相互竞争的说法。一种认为，在西方展出拯救了被威权政府压制的中国艺术家，使他们重新获得认可。另一种认为，这一现象代表了对社会主义中国艺术体系的彻底逆转，以及对“世界”的新开放。还有一种认为，它展示了中国在全球文化舞台上的民族胜利。的确，到2005年，中国在威尼斯双年展上有了自己的国家馆。
到2011年印度首次组织国家馆时，焦虑渗入了西方报道。《卫报》对这一时刻的报道开篇便带着一种隐隐的指责口吻：“中国和印度不满足于新兴经济超级大国的地位，正准备冲击一个非常欧洲的文化堡垒——威尼斯双年展。”

en: Ai Weiwei, the most globally recognized artist to emerge from this period, gained such stature
he crosscut and emblematized these narrative logics. He left China in 1981 and returned over a decade later with New York art world credibility. In 2000, he cocurated

, a satellite exhibit, shut down by authorities, to the first international Shanghai Biennale. By 2003 he was official consultant to the Swiss architecture firm Herzog and de Meuron on their design for the Beijing Olympics National “Bird’s Nest” stadium. He then flipped the state off—through public art projects critical of official hypocrisy and maleficence—with such flagrant style that he landed in jail.
He became the ultimate in bad boy political dissent, enabling the West to still feel edgy and free as exhibits like his 2014 @
stormed a decommissioned outpost of the U.S. prison industrial complex, rejuvenating the worn tourist attraction. Sometimes it seemed he was all that was left standing after the boom.
zh: 艾未未是这一时期涌现的最具全球知名度的艺术家，他之所以获得如此地位，是因为他横跨并象征了这些叙事逻辑。他1981年离开中国，十多年后带着纽约艺术界的资历归来。2000年，他与他人共同策划了首次国际化的上海双年展的外围展“不合作方式”（Fuck Off），该展被当局关闭。到2003年，他成为瑞士建筑事务所赫尔佐格和德梅隆设计北京奥运会国家“鸟巢”体育场的官方顾问。随后，他以极为张扬的风格向国家竖起了中指——通过批判官方虚伪与恶行的公共艺术项目——最终身陷囹圄。
他成为“坏男孩”政治异见的终极化身，使西方仍能自感前卫而自由，例如他2014年的展览“@Large：艾未未在阿尔卡特拉斯”闯入美国监狱工业复合体一处退役的前哨，让这个陈旧的旅游景点重获生机。有时看来，热潮过后，他是唯一还站立着的人。

en: challenges conventional narratives of rescue, reversal, or arrival through an ethnographic account of art world transition grounded in everyday experience and struggle rather than landmark exhibits and events. It examines the social role of art and competing ideas of aesthetic, cultural, and market value in reform-era China. And it does so with a feminist attentiveness to power dynamics in the work of art under the cultural conditions of late socialism–late liberalism that characterized China’s shifting position in the world.
zh: 《实验北京》挑战这些关于拯救、逆转或抵达的常规叙事。本书以日常经验与挣扎而非标志性展览和事件为基础，对艺术界的转型做民族志考察。它审视改革时代中国的艺术的社会角色，以及关于审美、文化和市场价值的相互竞争的观念。本书还带着女性主义对艺术劳动中权力动态的关注，将其置于晚期社会主义—晚期自由主义的文化条件中，正是这些条件塑造了中国在世界上不断变化的位置。

en: The conjunction of late socialism-late liberalism signals the interrelation of these two social projects from the 1980s on.

Under the leadership of Deng Xiaoping (1978–1989), the Chinese Communist Party (ccp) advanced the ideology of “Socialism with Chinese Characteristics,” which espoused market economics not as an abandonment of Marxism but as a commitment to the primary stage of socialism necessary for the future potentiality of communism. This reform of Maoist politics rejected the former utopian belief that modernization of productive forces through the market could be bypassed. With the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989 and the dissolution of the Soviet Union in 1991, the ccp legitimated its rule through new forms of governmentality and integration with neoliberalism as it unfolded in other parts of the world. State-owned enterprises were dismantled and sold off, and new public-private coalitions increasingly managed the provision of social services from housing to health care. Official institutions disseminated a wide-ranging discourse on

(quality) in which market success came to serve as the measure of individual and social value. Overall economic growth brought with it mounting material disparity and dispossession, as well as the suppression of protest in the name of social stability and the road to communism. Chinese neoliberalism provincialized the Western belief in market capitalism as linked with liberal democracy. The resulting crisis in legitimacy contributed to late liberalism, in which nations understood as liberal democracies justified their unequal distribution of livelihood through the invocation of cultural difference and need for civilizational securitization, in the name of future freedom for all.

documents this historical, experimental era in China, in which cultural production came to matter as a means of integration, legitimation, differentiation, and contestation. Some of the aesthetic experiments this moment gave rise to have become monumental, others ephemeral.
zh: 晚期社会主义与晚期自由主义的连接，标志着这两个社会工程自20世纪80年代以来的相互关联。

在邓小平（1978—1989）领导下，中国共产党提出“中国特色社会主义”意识形态，主张市场经济并非放弃马克思主义，而是对社会主义初级阶段的承诺，这个阶段是未来共产主义可能性所必需的。这场对毛泽东主义政治的改革，否定了先前那种认为可以绕过经由市场实现生产力现代化这一过程的乌托邦信念。随着1989年柏林墙倒塌和1991年苏联解体，中共通过新的治理形式，以及与世界其他地区展开的新自由主义相整合，为其统治取得合法性。国有企业被拆解、出售，新的公私联盟日益掌管从住房到医疗的社会服务供给。官方机构传播关于“素质”（suzhi）的广泛话语，市场成功由此成为衡量个人与社会价值的尺度。总体经济增长带来了日益加剧的物质不平等和剥夺，也带来了以社会稳定和通往共产主义之路为名的抗议压制。中国的新自由主义将西方关于市场资本主义与自由民主相联系的信念地方化了。由此产生的合法性危机助长了晚期自由主义：被理解为自由民主的国家通过援引文化差异和文明安全化的需要，以未来人人自由为名，为其不平等的生计分配辩护。《实验北京》记录了中国的这一历史的、实验性的时代——文化生产在其中成为整合、合法化、区分和抗争的手段。这一时刻所催生的审美实验，有些已成为纪念碑，另一些则转瞬即逝。

en: The global rise of Chinese contemporary art coincided with official efforts to stage spectacular international events, such as the Beijing Olympics in 2008 and the Shanghai World Expo in 2010, to attract the world’s attention and signal the end of a colonial first-world, third-world order of things. While often understood as distinct, mutually antagonistic realms of social activity, contemporary art and Chinese state politics increasingly overlapped. After the 1989 crackdown on protests in Tiananmen Square, a censorious attitude had characterized official response to contemporary art. During the lead-up to the Olympics, this circumspection gave way to a new market-driven, culture industry valuation of art. Experimental artists who felt the brunt of Cultural Bureau control throughout the 1990s, when Public Security officials routinely shut down “avant-garde” exhibits, suddenly found themselves courted to advance China’s image on the global stage.

Exhibition spaces generating new middle-class distinction eclipsed state-controlled museums whose dictate had been to exhibit the art of proletarian revolutionary nationalism. State planners, frequently operating in the changing economy as semicorporate entities, began to invite artists once lauded by foreign promoters as dissident visionaries to run new museums, create work for Beijing’s new airport, and design Olympic monuments, firework displays, and ceremony spectacles. The early years of the twenty-first century served as a turning point for Chinese contemporary art and a moment of continual reassessment and reflection by artists caught up in the processes of cultural marketization driven by intersecting local, national, and global forces.
zh: 中国当代艺术的全球崛起，恰逢官方努力举办壮观国际盛事——如2008年北京奥运会和2010年上海世博会——以吸引世界目光，宣告殖民式的第一世界/第三世界秩序终结。当代艺术与中国国家政治虽常被理解为彼此分离、相互对抗的社会活动领域，却日益交叠。1989年天安门广场抗议遭到镇压后，官方对当代艺术的回应一度以审查态度为特征。在奥运会筹备期间，这种谨慎让位于一种市场驱动、文化产业式的艺术估值。整个20世纪90年代，公安局官员经常关闭“前卫”展览，实验艺术家深受文化局控制之害；而此时，他们突然被拉拢来推进中国在全球舞台上的形象。
生产新中产阶级区隔的展览空间，盖过了受国家控制、以展出无产阶级革命民族主义艺术为指令的博物馆。国家规划者在变化的经济中往往以半企业实体的方式运作，开始邀请曾被外国推广者誉为异见先知的艺术家来经营新博物馆、为北京新机场创作、设计奥运纪念碑、烟火和仪式景观。21世纪初成为中国当代艺术的一个转折点，也是艺术家不断重新评估和反思的时刻——他们陷于由地方、国家与全球力量交汇驱动的文化市场化进程之中。

en: Their activity, centered in China’s rapidly transforming “global cities,” occurred in tandem with revaluations of rural and urban space, public and private boundaries, and masculinity and femininity.

Through participant observation from 2000 to 2002, predominantly in Beijing, I came to understand Chinese contemporary art not as a bounded object but a zone of cultural encounter in which these revaluations were represented, worked out, and questioned. Its participants included artists, officials, urban planners, cultural consultants, and art professionals from around the world who, in repeated encounters in China and abroad, negotiated what counts as Chinese and what counts as art. In debates about women and art, they negotiated what counts as feminist. While the frame of encounter ostensibly characterizes this early twenty-first-century moment, how artists navigated shifting flows of art discourse also reveals historical encounters and contradictions in understandings of what art is meant to do. As I detail in the three parts of this book—Art Worldings, Zones of Encounter, and Feminist Sight Lines—artists adapted to the changing ideological context for art production but not without a struggle over the politics of form and how it positioned them in relation to the nation and the world, the past and the future.
zh: 他们的活动以中国迅速转型的“全球城市”为中心，与对城乡空间、公私边界以及男性气质和女性气质的重新估价同步发生。

2000年至2002年，我主要在北京进行参与观察，逐渐认识到中国当代艺术不是一个有边界的对象，而是一个文化相遇地带（zone of encounter）。这些重新估价在其中被再现、协商和质疑。其参与者包括艺术家、官员、城市规划者、文化顾问以及来自世界各地的艺术专业人士；他们在中国和国外的反复相遇中，协商什么算中国的、什么算艺术。在关于女性与艺术的争论中，他们协商什么算女性主义的。相遇的框架表面上描述了21世纪初这一时刻，但艺术家如何穿行于艺术话语的流动变化，也揭示了历史性的相遇，以及关于艺术应做什么的理解中的矛盾。正如我在本书三个部分——艺术世界营造、相遇地带、女性主义视线——中详述的，艺术家适应了艺术生产不断变化的意识形态语境，但这一过程伴随着围绕形式政治及形式如何将他们置于民族与世界、过去与未来关系中的斗争。

en: At Large in the Global City
zh: 逍遥于全球城市

en: Wang Nengtao’s 2002 panoramic photograph
captures the scale of construction that permeated Beijing, as well as other Chinese megacities, at the turn of the millennium (plate 1).

Massive yellow cranes punctuate the scene. They jut into the sky and recede in grey tones toward a smoggy horizon. In the expanse of worksites below, demarcated by green mesh fencing, sandbag walls, and piles of rebar, workers in yellow helmets appear miniature. The piece’s long horizontal format resembles a traditional Chinese scroll painting, but rather than inviting the viewer’s eye to meander through a natural landscape, with resting spots along the way for reflection, its perspectival, photographic realism insists on a survey from above, of an anonymous multitude turning over the earth in an ideological remaking—a re-worlding—of Chinese social life.
Wang’s title hints at how such monumental efforts destabilized past political projects, of Communist Party class revolution and agrarian reform, as well as everyday existence in a city like Beijing.
zh: 王能涛2002年的全景摄影《颠覆——土地》捕捉了世纪之交弥漫北京的建造规模，也捕捉了中国其他特大城市的景象（图版1）。

巨大的黄色起重机点缀着画面。它们伸向天空，在灰色调中向着烟雾迷蒙的地平线退去。下方广阔工地上，绿色网栏、沙袋墙和成堆钢筋划出区域，戴黄色头盔的工人显得十分微小。作品的长横幅格式类似中国传统卷轴画，但它并不邀请观者的目光在自然景观中蜿蜒游走、沿途驻足沉思；其透视性的摄影写实主义坚持从高处俯视，俯视无数无名者在意识形态的再造——一次再世界营造（re-worlding）——中翻掘大地，重塑中国的社会生活。
王能涛的标题暗示，这种规模宏大的努力如何动摇了过去的政治工程——共产党的阶级革命和土地改革——以及北京这类城市中的日常生活。

en: In my field notes from the same year, I posed a question about the relationship between contemporary art and Beijing: Am I trying to write an ethnography about a city in which art plays a part or an ethnography about art in which the city plays a part? This book explores the questions that unfolded from that one. How do aesthetics do more than simply reflect political, social, and economic change? How does cultural production, as once theorized by Chinese Communist intellectuals, actively shape collective consciousness and social identity, perceptions of time and space, and visions of the world? What is the legacy of past forms of visual praxis on contemporary production? How are envisioned timespaces always-already uneven and gendered? The construction site in

provides a metaphor for a central tension in my account of Chinese contemporary art during the first years of the new millennium: between the power of art to represent, at large or from above, a cultural entity like Beijing or China or even the world and the potentially subversive activity of the artist, at large in its streets and alleys, monuments and ruins, lived histories and intimate interiors.
zh: 在同年田野笔记中，我提出一个关于当代艺术与北京关系的问题：我究竟是在写一部艺术在其中扮演角色的城市民族志，还是在写一部城市在其中扮演角色的艺术民族志？本书探讨由这个问题展开的一系列问题。美学如何不只是简单反映政治、社会和经济变化？文化生产——正如中国共产党知识分子曾经理论化的那样——如何主动塑造集体意识和社会身份、对时间和空间的感知，以及对世界的想象？过去的视觉实践形式在当代生产中留下了什么遗产？被构想出的时空如何总是已经不均匀，并且被性别化？《颠覆——土地》中的工地，为我叙述新千年最初几年中国当代艺术提供了一个核心张力的隐喻：一边是艺术从整体上或从高处再现北京、中国乃至世界这类文化实体的力量，另一边是艺术家在大街小巷、纪念碑与废墟、生活历史与私密内室中逍遥游荡、可能具有颠覆性的活动。

en: As I traversed streets plastered with slogans like “New Century, New Beijing,” I practiced, in my minor and temporary way, something most residents did. I mapped the city and my relationship to it, to what had been, to what was marked for demolition, to what was being torn down, and to what was being built. People talked all the time about the

(demolition and relocation) politics of urban renewal ubiquitous in Chinese cities, about the logic or the injustice of it, about how favorite haunts had disappeared overnight or how they could no longer find their way around once familiar neighborhoods. Some artists seized the moment as an opportunity to move out of the studio—with still and video cameras, spray paint, mirrors, bricks, fabric, ice, and their own bodies—to create site-specific works about this epochal process.
zh: 当我穿行于贴满“新世纪、新北京”之类标语的街道时，我以自己微小而短暂的方式，实践着大多数居民都在做的事。我绘制城市，也绘制我与城市的关系，与曾经存在之物、与标记为待拆之物、与正在被推倒之物和正在建起之物的关系。人们不断谈论中国城市中无处不在的城市更新拆迁（chaiqian）政治，谈论其中的逻辑或不公，谈论心爱的去处如何一夜之间消失，或他们如何再也认不出曾经熟悉的街区。一些艺术家抓住这一刻，走出画室——带着照相机和摄像机、喷漆、镜子、砖块、布料、冰以及自己的身体——创作关于这一划时代进程的特定场域作品。

en: I tracked their role in China’s endeavor to “link tracks with the world” (

). In 2001 alone, China entered the wto, Beijing won its bid to host the 2008 Olympics, and the men’s national soccer team qualified for the first time to compete in the 2002 World Cup. This sequence of events briefly gave rise to the phrase

, meaning “to enter the world,” or in a pun playing on the Chinese homophones of world and city, “to enter the city.” This conflation of Beijing, China, and the world shimmered with the anticipation of having finally arrived. It played off of, even as it diminished, the Maoist commitment to “enter the life” (

) of the exploited classes and rural peasantry in order to represent them. Urbanism, the privileging of city over country as site of growth, excitement, and futurity, became the mandate of the day. I followed artists and their interlocutors from art classrooms to cramped apartment studios to an expanding number of local exhibition spaces, through a city that many likened to a massive construction zone. Male rural migrants labored night and day on the skeletons of high-rise buildings. Migrant women worked in restaurants, hair salons, entertainment spaces, and private homes. Urban workers laid off from “iron-rice-bowl” jobs in state-owned enterprises struggled to survive in a new market economy. Students and strivers from the provinces, expats from Hong Kong, Taiwan, Korea, Japan, and beyond entered this border zone of city and country, socialism and capitalism, nation and world, memory and dream. Dust hung in the air. Cranes swung through the sky. The chemical smell of urban renewal wafted through the streets.
zh: 我追踪他们在中国努力“与世界接轨”（yu shijie jiegui）中的角色。仅2001年一年，中国加入世贸组织，北京赢得2008年奥运会主办权，国家男子足球队首次获得2002年世界杯参赛资格。这一连串事件短暂催生了“入世”一词——意为“进入世界”，又借“世”与“市”的中文同音双关，可读作“进入城市”。北京、中国与世界三者的这种融合，因终于抵达的期待而闪闪发光。它借用、甚至削弱了毛泽东主义关于“深入生活”（shenru shenghuo）、即深入被剥削阶级和农村农民生活以再现他们的承诺。城市主义——把城市而非乡村视为增长、兴奋与未来的场所——成为时代任务。我跟随艺术家及其对话者，从艺术教室到逼仄的公寓画室，再到数量不断扩张的地方展览空间，穿行于一座被许多人比作巨大工地的城市。男性农村移民在高楼骨架上日夜劳作。女性移民在餐馆、发廊、娱乐场所和私人住宅中工作。从国有企业“铁饭碗”岗位下岗的城市工人，在新的市场经济中艰难求生。来自各省的学生和奋斗者，从香港、台湾、韩国、日本及其他地方移居而来的人，进入这座城乡之间、社会主义与资本主义之间、民族与世界之间、记忆与梦想之间的边界地带。尘土悬在空中。起重机在头顶摆动。城市更新的化学气味在街道上飘荡。

en: China’s transition from a socialist political economy toward integration with transnational capitalism affected visual art production in numerous ways. The state relaxed orthodox political authority over art, although this process was intermittent and not without reversal. As state stipends dwindled, artists sought new channels of support and commission. Many threw themselves into experimenting with aesthetic form and found themselves navigating emergent market forces. Chinese contemporary art began to circulate in international and developing domestic markets, becoming subject to multiple modes of interpretation and evaluation. Art academies and exhibition spaces underwent reorganization and semiprivatization. The artists I came to know negotiated this nexus of state cultural control, market economics, and gender politics in the attempt to earn a living and make and exhibit their work.
zh: 中国从社会主义政治经济向跨国资本主义整合的转型，以多种方式影响了视觉艺术生产。国家放松了对艺术的正统政治权威，尽管这一过程时断时续，也并非没有反复。随着国家补贴减少，艺术家寻找新的支持和委托渠道。许多人投身审美形式实验，发现自己要在新兴市场力量中摸索前行。中国当代艺术开始在国际市场和发展中的国内市场流通，受到多种解释和评价模式的支配。美术院校和展览空间经历重组与半私有化。我逐渐认识的艺术家们，在国家文化控制、市场经济与性别政治的交汇处协商，努力谋生、创作和展出作品。

en: By and large, they belonged to an in-between generation, born between the late 1950s and early 1970s, whose experiences spanned the transition from socialism to “reform and opening.” They had some personal memory of the Cultural Revolution; some had even been sent-down youth who spent years in the countryside. Many had trained in China’s top national art academies, in Beijing, Hangzhou, or Chongqing, where they mastered the techniques of socialist realism, even if they later discarded these for experiments in performance, installation, or video art. Some waxed nostalgic over the “culture fever” (
) years of the 1980s, when they gained access to texts, theories, and forms of art suppressed under Mao and immersed themselves in intense debates that went on late into the night.

They had lived through the cultural and political crackdown after the 1989 protests in Tiananmen Square. They had witnessed the impact of accelerating market reforms after Deng Xiaoping’s 1992 Tour of the South and pronouncement that China link tracks with the world through trade. As the millennial premise of Beijing as global city came to increasingly depend on the development of a cultural economy rather than an industrial one, they got caught up, energized and conflicted by this new relationship between capital and culture. Their paths through the city traced a network that extended in new ways to other parts of China and the world, the past and the present. Their experiences, stories, artworks, and actions mapped discrepant transnational connections across space and time. How these maps were drawn depended on social positionality, with coordinates shaped by gender, class, and rural-urban identity.
zh: 总的来说，他们属于夹在中间的一代，出生于20世纪50年代末到70年代初，其经历横跨从社会主义到“改革开放”的转型。他们对文化大革命还有个人记忆；有些人甚至当过知青，在乡下度过数年。许多人曾在中国顶尖的国立美术院校——北京、杭州或重庆——受训，掌握了社会主义现实主义技法，尽管后来为了行为、装置或录像艺术实验而抛弃了这些技法。有些人对20世纪80年代的“文化热”（wenhua re）岁月满怀怀念，那时他们得以接触毛泽东时代被压制的文本、理论和艺术形式，沉浸在持续到深夜的激烈辩论中。

他们经历过1989年天安门广场抗议之后的文化和政治镇压。他们见证了邓小平1992年南方视察并宣布通过贸易与世界接轨后加速市场化改革的影响。随着北京作为全球城市的千禧年构想日益依赖文化经济而非工业经济的发展，他们被资本与文化之间的这种新关系所裹挟，既充满能量又充满矛盾。他们在城市中的路径，编织出一张网络以新的方式伸向中国其他地方和世界、过去与现在。他们的经历、故事、作品和行动，绘制出跨越空间与时间的差异化的跨国连接。这些地图如何绘制取决于社会位置，其坐标由性别、阶级和城乡身份塑造。

en: Gender in the Global City
zh: 全球城市中的性别

en: If Wang Nengtao’s
captures the massive turning over of the urban landscape, Yin Xiuzhen’s 2001

(figure Intro.01) packs it into a suitcase. Displayed on the floor, the suitcase lies open to reveal frame-supported fabric, cut and engineered to resemble architectural elements of the cityscape. The small, rumpled, and soft structures interject the alienating modern megacity with the domestic intimacy of human wear and dwelling.

Made from clothing once worn by the artist and her family members, the piece represents Beijing as a ring of buildings circling the open green space of a stretched shirt. Pulled inward, the sleeve leads the viewer’s eye down to a macro lens that displays in miniature a map of the city circa 1949 affixed to the bottom of the suitcase. A speaker inside plays Beijing opera sung by elderly amateurs recorded in Shichahai Park, a popular public space north of the Forbidden City flooded by 2001 with trendy restaurants, bars, and bicycle rickshaw tours of old
alleyways.
zh: 如果说王能涛的《颠覆》捕捉了城市景观的大规模翻掘，尹秀珍2001年的《便携城市——北京》（导论图01）则把它装进一只手提箱。手提箱摊开在地面，露出由框架支撑的布料，这些布料经剪裁和设计，形似城市景观的建筑元素。那些小巧、皱褶、柔软的结构，以人体穿着与栖居的居家亲密感，插入这座令人疏离的现代特大城市。
作品用艺术家及其家人穿过的旧衣制成，把北京表现为一环建筑，环绕着一件被拉抻的衬衫所呈现的绿色空地。袖子被向内拉，引导观者的视线向下落到一枚微距镜头上，镜头在微缩中显示一张约1949年的北京地图，贴在箱底。箱内扬声器播放着老年业余爱好者在什刹海公园唱的京剧录音；什刹海是故宫以北的热门公共空间，2001年时已被时尚餐馆、酒吧和老胡同三轮车游览挤满。

en: The only recognizable building is the Central Radio and tv Tower, which marks the suitcase’s outer rim as the Third Ring Road. All of central Beijing has disappeared in a taut expanse of green fabric pulled into a slightly off-center vortex with a diminishing view of the historical capital. This timehole, with its soundtrack of disembodied Beijing opera singers, eerily empties the center, a site of massive razing and rebuilding, including the soon-to-be-demolished hutong where Yin and her artist husband Song Dong lived during the creation of this piece. Within a few years, its defining monument would be outdated, surpassed in size, ambition, and international reputation by the new China Central Television Headquarters designed by Rem Koolhaas as anchor to Beijing’s new Central Business District.
serves as a premonition of the accelerating changes to come, while also giving shelter to the tactility of memory and personal history.
zh: 唯一可辨认的建筑是中央广播电视塔，它标记着手提箱外缘即三环路。整个北京中心在绷紧的绿色布料中消失，布料被拉成一个略偏中心的漩涡，历史首都的视野随之缩小。这个时间空洞伴随着只闻其声、不见其人的京剧演唱，令人不安地掏空了城市中心；那里是大规模拆建之地，包括尹秀珍和她的艺术家丈夫宋冬创作这件作品时居住的、不久将被拆除的胡同。几年之内，这座标志性建筑就会显得过时，在规模、雄心和国际声誉上被雷姆·库哈斯设计的新中央电视台总部超越——后者成为北京新中央商务区的锚点。《便携北京》预示了即将到来且不断加速的变化，同时也庇护着记忆与个人历史的触感。

en: was the first in what became a series titled
. As Yin Xiuzhen began receiving commissions to create new works in locations around the world, she frequently found herself in transit. The idea for
came to her while waiting at an airport baggage claim, when she suddenly saw each suitcase as the home a traveler tries to carry with her.

She fabricated the pieces in the series from old clothing gathered at their respective sites of creation: Shanghai, Singapore, Sydney, New York, Berlin, Paris.... As these portable cities accumulated, Yin began to exhibit them as an ensemble mapping her travels (figure Intro.02). On an oceanic blue wall behind the open suitcases, yellow buttons serve as drop pins for each city, connected by strands of yellow yarn. While Beijing now appears as one among many networked global destinations, the familial specificity of the clothing in this first in series activates a different emotional energy, linking materiality and memory. Each piece of fabric evoked personal details of wear, care, and the passage of time. Yin recalled, for example, that she’d created a purple building from a shirt she once thought was very fashionable when her sister gave it to her.

She has also discussed how the act of sewing so central to her artistic practice produced a connection with her mother, who once worked in a clothing factory and sometimes took up needle and thread to help Yin with her artwork.
as the point of origin for

stitches together intergenerational histories of home and state: of women’s virtue performed through needlework as emblem of domesticity, of female labor mobilized into socialist industrial production, and of gendered global commodity chains. It vacillates between the touch and feel of home and everywhere-nowhere market reproducibility.
zh: 《便携北京》是后来名为《便携城市》系列的第一件。随着尹秀珍开始接到在世界各地创作新作品的委托，她经常处于旅途之中。《便携城市》的构想是她在机场行李提取处等候时产生的——她忽然把每只手提箱都看作旅行者试图随身携带的家。

她用从各创作地收集来的旧衣制作这个系列的作品：上海、新加坡、悉尼、纽约、柏林、巴黎……随着这些便携城市不断累积，尹秀珍开始把它们作为整体展出，绘制出她的旅行地图（导论图02）。在敞开的手提箱背后那片海洋蓝色的墙上，黄色纽扣作为每座城市的地图图钉，由黄毛线连接。北京现在只是众多联网全球目的地之一，但这一系列中第一件作品的衣物所承载的家庭具体性，激发出另一种情感能量，把物质性与记忆连接起来。每块布料都唤起关于穿着、照料和时间流逝的个人细节。例如，尹秀珍回忆道，她用一件衬衫做了一座紫色建筑，当年她的姐妹把这件衬衫送给她时，她觉得它非常时髦。
她也谈过，缝纫这一在她艺术实践中居于核心的行为，如何把她与母亲连接起来——母亲曾在服装厂工作，有时会拿起针线帮尹秀珍做作品。
作为《便携城市》的起点，《便携北京》缝合起关于家与国家的代际历史：女性通过针线活操演美德，作为居家的象征；女性劳动被动员进社会主义工业生产；以及性别化的全球商品链。《便携北京》在家的触摸与感觉和无处不在又无处可寻的市场可复制性之间摇摆。

, 2001. Installation. Courtesy of the artist.
zh: 导论图01　尹秀珍，《便携城市——北京》，2001年。装置。艺术家惠允。

en: INTRO.02 Yin Xiuzhen,
, 2002–present. Installation view, Yin Xiuzhen solo exhibition, Groninger Museum, Netherlands, 2012. Courtesy of the artist.
zh: 导论图02　尹秀珍，《便携城市》，2002年至今。装置现场，尹秀珍个展，格罗宁根博物馆，荷兰，2012年。艺术家惠允。

en: If Wang Nengtao’s
and Yin Xiuzhen’s
ruminate on China’s capital as construction site and global city in the making, in which art and urbanism are articulated together, Chen Lingyang’s

continues their study of scale, with a cityscape haunted by gender politics (plate 2). In this photographic dreamspace, one in a two-piece series, a nude giantess looms within Beijing’s built environment. The angle of perspective in the long scroll-like photograph, as in Wang’s, comes from above, although here the only visible human figure miniaturizes the buildings. It is the artist’s own body at the center of the image, lying face down on top of an apartment block, her exposed spine aligned with its central axis. Her head dangles over the edge, hair hanging down like that of an ink brush. The female figure appears huge yet vulnerable, as she comes into sensuous contact with a city where new commercial buildings rise above socialist work-unit housing. Exhibited as a transparency in an illuminated lightbox, the image glows with a dark, magic-hour intensity. Of this series, Chen comments: “Very often, the real world and the male world get mixed up in my mind. They both come from outside me; they both exist very forcefully, with initiative, power, and aggression. Facing these two worlds, I often feel that I am weak and helpless, and don’t know what to do. But just being alive means that I cannot avoid them, not even for one day. I wish that every day there could be a certain time like 25:00, when I could become as large as I like, and do whatever I want.”
This larger-than-life figuration exists in temporal ephemerality.
zh: 如果说王能涛的《颠覆》和尹秀珍的《便携北京》思考的是作为工地和形成中的全球城市的中国首都——艺术与城市主义在其中被一起表述——那么陈羚羊的《25:00》延续了它们对尺度的研究，呈现一个被性别政治萦绕的城市景观（图版2）。在这幅摄影梦境空间（由两件作品构成的系列中的一件）中，一个裸体的女巨人隐现在北京的建筑环境中。与王能涛的作品一样，这幅长卷式照片的视角来自上方，不过这里唯一可见的人形使建筑显得微小。那是艺术家自己的身体，位于图像中心，俯卧在一栋公寓楼顶上，裸露的脊柱与楼的中央轴线对齐。她的头悬在边缘，头发垂下如毛笔。这个女性形象看似巨大，却脆弱，她与一座城市发生感官接触，那里新的商业建筑高耸于社会主义单位住房之上。作品作为透明胶片在发光的灯箱中展出，影像以幽暗的“魔幻时刻”强度闪耀。关于这个系列，陈羚羊说：“现实世界和男性世界常常在我头脑中混在一起。它们都来自我之外；它们都非常强力地存在，带着主动性、力量和侵略性。面对这两个世界，我常常觉得自己软弱无助，不知道该怎么办。但只是活着就意味着我无法回避它们，一天也不行。我希望每天都能有像25:00这样的某个时刻，让我想变多大就变多大，想做什么就做什么。”
这个超越真人大小的形象存在于时间性的短暂之中。

en: raises questions about the politics of representation in Chinese contemporary art: about how gender matters in terms of art world access and recognition; how art shapes understandings of femininity and masculinity; and how gender and sexuality figure centrally in conceptions of China’s modernity and worldliness. While several important historical accounts document Chinese contemporary art from the 1980s on, questions of gender and feminism in them remain an afterthought, relegated to single chapters or subsections of these thick volumes.

Informed by a rich body of scholarship that has demonstrated the significance of precisely these questions in China’s development as a modern nation-state, its revolutionary politics and market reform,
confronts this sidelining of gender in the story of art.

It asks what a focus on gender, as central rather than epiphenomenal, reveals about an emerging art world. In the next section, an overview of influential exhibits from the two decades preceding the new millennium provides historical context. The politics of representation that played out in these exhibits, inside and outside of China, resulted in a new artistic political grammar.
Avant-garde became coded as
(hooligan) and masculine.
Female artists, largely excluded from this realm of activity, found their work contained within a new domesticating and marginalizing category of

(feminine or women’s art). My feminist intent throughout this book is to deconstruct this restrictive, binaristic liumang/nüxing political grammar in order to make a new form of storytelling possible.
zh: 《25:00》提出了关于中国当代艺术再现政治的问题：性别在艺术界的进入与承认方面如何重要；艺术如何塑造对女性气质与男性气质的理解；性别与性如何在中国现代性与世界性的构想中占据中心位置。尽管已有若干重要的历史著述记录20世纪80年代以来的中国当代艺术，但其中的性别与女性主义问题仍属事后附笔，被降格为这些厚重著作中的单一章节或小节。
有丰富的学术成果已经证明，恰恰是这些问题在中国作为现代民族国家的发展、革命政治与市场改革中具有重要意义；《实验北京》以此为参照，直面艺术叙事中对性别的边缘化。
本书追问，当性别被置于中心而非附带现象的位置，它能揭示一个新兴艺术界的什么。下一节将概述新千年之前二十年间有影响力的展览，以提供历史语境。这些展览在中国内外展开的再现政治，形成了一种新的艺术政治语法。
前卫被编码为流氓（liumang）和男性气质。
女性艺术家大体被排除在这一活动领域之外，她们的作品被收进一个新的、驯化且边缘化的“女性艺术”（nüxing yishu）范畴。本书贯穿始终的女性主义意图，是解构这种限制性的、二元对立的流氓/女性政治语法，从而让一种新的讲故事形式成为可能。

en: Exhibition Politics
zh: 展览政治

en: On February 5, 1989,

opened in Beijing at the National Art Museum of China. Six long black banners draped down the entrance stairs announced the exhibition title and displayed the red and white insignia of a no U-turn sign. This survey show, including 297 pieces by 186 artists, represented a culmination of the many art activities and groups that had emerged over the previous decade.
In 1979, several unofficial art exhibits, building on the energy of the Beijing Spring Democracy Movement, attracted broad attention. The

remains the best known of these efforts. Staged on the street outside of the National Art Museum, it featured work by young artists with little to no formal training. Art colleges had been shut throughout the Cultural Revolution and only began to readmit students in 1978. Some of the work by the Stars group explicitly attacked Maoist ideology, and police shut the exhibit down after two days. Stars members responded by holding a public demonstration on October 1, the thirtieth anniversary of the founding of the People’s Republic of China. By the mid-1980s, intellectual debates about reestablishing humanism in the aftermath of the Cultural Revolution and art trends such as the normalization of nudity in painting signaled an ongoing liberalization of culture. Numerous unofficial art groups and interlocutors of Western modernist styles sprouted up around the country. This efflorescence of artistic experiments and theories eventually became known at the ’85 Art New Wave.
zh: 1989年2月5日，中国现代艺术展（China/Avant-Garde）在北京中国美术馆开幕。六条长长的黑色横幅从入口台阶垂下，宣告展览标题，并展示红白两色的“禁止掉头”标志。这场汇集186位艺术家297件作品的综述展，代表了此前十年间涌现的众多艺术活动和群体的顶点。

1979年，几场非官方艺术展借北京之春民主运动的能量吸引了广泛关注。星星美展仍是这些努力中最著名的一例。展览在中国美术馆外的街道上举行，展出几乎没有受过正规训练的年轻艺术家的作品。文化大革命期间美术院校全部停办，直到1978年才开始重新招生。星星画会的一些作品明确抨击毛泽东主义意识形态，警方在两天后关闭了展览。星星成员于10月1日——中华人民共和国成立三十周年——举行公开示威作为回应。到20世纪80年代中期，关于在文化大革命之后重建人道主义的知识界辩论，以及绘画中裸体正常化等艺术潮流，标志着文化持续自由化。众多非官方艺术团体和西方现代主义风格的呼应者在全国各地涌现。这场艺术实验和理论的繁盛最终被称为“85美术新潮”。

en: By the time of the

exhibition, interest in this burgeoning art scene had developed in China. As audience members, who had turned out on the eve of Chinese New Year, wandered through the galleries, two shots rang out. Artist Xiao Lu had drawn a handgun and fired into her piece

, shattering a mirror at the center of the installation. Police arrested her and Tang Song, another artist at the scene whom they assumed was involved, and closed the exhibit. It reopened several days later, only to be suspended one more time due to pieces in violation of the organizers’ contract with the museum not to exhibit performance art, as well as a false bomb threat. Nonetheless, it came to be known as an important retrospective of the artistic energies unleashed during the 1980s, and from the perspective of many I met during my fieldwork, the last interesting thing to happen at the National Art Museum of China. Just three months after the exhibit, the growing student protests in Tiananmen Square captured international media attention. Following the events of June 4, 1989, authorities shut down several prominent art magazines, and artists who had participated in
experienced difficulty showing in official venues. Some, like Xiao Lu and Tang Song, left the country.
zh: 到中国现代艺术展举办时，中国国内对这蓬勃艺术场景的兴趣已经发展起来。观众在农历新年前夕前来观展，在展厅间游荡时，两声枪响响起。艺术家肖鲁掏出手枪，朝自己的作品《对话》开枪，击碎了装置中央的一面镜子。警方逮捕了她和现场另一名艺术家唐宋——他们以为他也参与其中——并关闭了展览。几天后展览重开，却因有作品违反主办方与美术馆签订的不展出行为艺术的协议，以及一次虚假炸弹威胁，再次被暂停。尽管如此，它仍被视为20世纪80年代释放的艺术能量的重要回顾展；从我田野调查中遇到的许多人来看，这是中国美术馆发生的最后一件有趣的事。展览仅仅三个月后，天安门广场上不断增长的学生抗议吸引了国际媒体注意。1989年6月4日事件之后，当局关闭了几本知名艺术杂志，参与中国现代艺术展的艺术家在官方场所展出遭遇困难。一些人，如肖鲁和唐宋，离开了中国。

en: In the climate of tension and uncertainty that ensued, officials viewed Chinese art labeled “avant-garde” as a suspect manifestation of liberal bourgeois tendencies. With equal conviction, the international art market embraced it as an emblem of resistance to authoritarian oppression.
During the 1990s, this art toured an ever-widening international circuit.

artists, opened at the Hong Kong Arts Centre and City Hall in 1993. Co-organized by Beijing critic and curator Li Xianting and Hong Kong art collector Chang Tsong-zung, it shaped international knowledge of Chinese contemporary art and the careers of a select group of almost exclusively male artists. After Hong Kong, a scaled-down version traveled to London, Sydney, and Melbourne, and from 1995 to 1998 to the North American cities of Vancouver; Eugene, Oregon; Fort Wayne, Indiana; Salina, Kansas; Chicago; and San Jose, California. Other exhibitions in Europe—

children: China Avant-Garde: Counter-Currents in Art and Culture

en: (1993) in Berlin,
